fields.meta_description: Build a shipping form that collects the billing account and customs details your dock needs. Every request is saved to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Shipping Form With Every Detail the Dock Needs
fields.hero_description: Describe what gets shipped and who pays for it. Emergent builds the shipping form, applies your desk's rules to each request, and saves every one to a table you own.
fields.features_heading: What Each Request Carries to the Dock
fields.features_subheading: A printed request stops at blank lines. These six pieces let the desk book a carrier without writing back to ask.
fields.feature_1:
A billing account on every request

Require the grant, cost center or client code each shipment is charged to. The desk books the carrier knowing who pays, and finance matches every charge to the request behind it.
fields.feature_2:
Rules your shipping desk already follows

Route a request by its weight or destination, or hold it until the right day. Describe the rule in plain English once, and the form applies it to each request that follows.
fields.feature_3:
Customs fields that appear only for export

Show customs fields only when the destination is outside the US, with a tariff code and value required per line. Domestic requests stay short, and export ones reach the desk whole.
fields.feature_4:
Photos and packing lists kept together

Let packers attach a photo of the sealed carton and requesters upload a packing list. Files sit with the request in your database, where the dock finds them without an inbox search.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts that reach whoever books it

Post each new request to a Slack channel, or email it to the person who books the carrier. Each alert carries the account and the service level the desk needs to book the shipment.
fields.feature_6:
The whole codebase, exported

Export the code to GitHub on paid plans when the shipping form needs to live inside your warehouse system. The form, its rules, and the requests table are yours to host and change.
fields.why_title: Why Build Shipping Forms With Emergent?
fields.why_description: A downloaded template collects an address and a weight. Billing and customs checks still happen by hand at the dock.

fields.tab_content_1:
Frozen samples wait for Monday instead of a weekend dock

Researchers at Cedar Hills University ship through one form that needs a grant account number. Frozen samples requested on a Thursday or Friday wait until Monday. The Hale Lab asks to ship 6 tubes of plasma on Thursday, and the request sits at the top of Monday's mailroom queue.
fields.tab_content_2:
Anything over 50 lb leaves on the freight dock

Packers at Northwind Supply fill in a dispatch checklist on a tablet before sealing a carton, with the weight typed off the scale. Anything over 50 lb goes to the freight desk instead of parcel pickup. Order 20417 comes in at 58 lb and moves to the freight lead's queue.
fields.tab_content_3:
Export requests carry an HS code for each line

Nothing leaves Lumen Audio for another country until every line has an HS code and a value. The sales rep fills those in, and the form totals the values into a commercial invoice PDF for the shipping desk. Two A-40 amplifiers and a cable set for a Rotterdam dealer come to $2,460.
fields.tab_content_4:
Booth freight leaves 12 days ahead of the show

Booth crates at Globex Software ship 12 days before a trade show opens. The coordinator enters the show date and the venue's receiving address, and the form sets the ship-by date. Each request posts to #events in Slack. For a show that opens in 20 days, the crates go out within 8.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Shipping Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the questions your shipping desk keeps asking, then write the answers into the form.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Read through the last month of emails between requesters and the shipping desk. Every question the desk had to ask, such as a missing suite number or an unclear package size, becomes a required field on the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the accounts each shipment can be charged to, whether grant numbers, cost centers, or client codes. Put them in a dropdown instead of a free text box, and every request arrives with an account finance recognizes.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write down the rules the desk works by today, such as a weight that means freight or a day frozen goods never leave. Each one becomes a condition on the form instead of something a new hire learns by mistake.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide which fields only international requests need. A tariff code and a value per line belong there, along with the recipient's phone number. Domestic requesters never see them, and their form stays short.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt with the fields, the accounts, and the rules in plain English. Emergent builds the shipping form and a requests table behind it. Change any of it later by asking, such as adding a new service level.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose where new requests go: a Slack channel the dock watches, or an email to whoever books the carrier. Rush requests can alert the person on call, while ground shipments wait in the daily queue the desk works through each morning.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with an awkward request
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form in yourself with an export of two lines and one heavy carton before anyone else sees it. Check that the weight rule fired, then find the request in the table under the right account.

plan.angle: The live top 10 mixes builder templates (Jotform's shipping checklist, forms.app's shipping order form, a Google Form shipping report) with a university's printed shipping request PDF and image galleries. None of them shows what happens after someone fills the form in: who books the carrier, which account pays, what customs paperwork the item needs. This page treats a shipping form as the internal request that reaches a shipping desk complete, answers the PAA questions about shipping documents and shipping terms plainly, and shows four teams whose requests carry different rules: a research lab's weekend hold, a warehouse weight check, export paperwork and trade show deadlines. Customer checkout and purchase orders stay on the order form and purchase order form siblings.
tab_stories: A researcher at Cedar Hills University requests a frozen sample shipment on a Thursday, the form charges it to a grant account and holds it to Monday under the core's no-weekend rule, and the mailroom sees it in Monday's queue.

A packer at Northwind Supply works through a dispatch checklist on a tablet, enters a carton weight of 58 lb, and the form routes that carton to the freight desk because the warehouse sends anything over 50 lb there.

An export request at Lumen Audio needs an HS code, a country of origin and a value for every line before it submits, and the shipping desk receives a commercial invoice PDF that adds the lines up to $2,460.

A marketing coordinator at Globex Software books booth freight for a trade show, the form works out a ship-by date 12 days before the show opens, and the request posts to #events in Slack with that date.

claims_to_source: A bill of lading (BOL) is a transportation document that serves as a receipt for the goods, a contract of carriage and evidence of title, listing the goods shipped and the delivery terms

A commercial invoice is used by customs to determine the value of goods when assessing duties, and an export packing list itemizes quantities, package types, weights and marks; it does not replace the commercial invoice

Harmonized System (HS) codes are a standardized numerical method, developed by the World Customs Organization, that classifies traded goods at six digits, with countries adding digits for 8- or 10-digit codes
Incoterms are rules published by the International Chamber of Commerce that set buyer and seller responsibilities for delivery, costs and risk, such as FOB, EXW and DDP
LTL (less than truckload) freight shares trailer space with other shippers' freight, while FTL (full truckload) uses a whole trailer for one shipment
The main ways to move freight are road, rail, air and ocean
